soc-2.system_description: Prestige Worldwide Licensing Platform: a multi-tenant SaaS application that lets broadcasters and agencies search, license and download media assets, with rights metadata, contract terms and royalty reporting. Customer commitment: 99.9% monthly availability. In the boundary: the web app and public APIs, licensing metadata and customer file stores, CI/CD pipeline, identity provider, SIEM and backup tooling, and the people and processes that run them. Out of the boundary: the public cloud provider (carved-out subservice organization; physical and infrastructure controls rely on its SOC report), the payment processor, corporate finance systems and the marketing website.

framework_assessments.implementation:
OVERVIEW
Prestige Worldwide reports practices addressing CC1.1 — Ethical conduct within the selected system. This is reported readiness, not evidence verification or an auditor opinion.

IMPLEMENTATION BREAKDOWN
Ethical expectations
- Conduct expectations and communication: reported in place — Alice briefs staff and project contractors on honest rights clearance, confidential media handling and reporting concerns before access is granted; Derek repeats the expectations at creative-project intake.

Leadership in practice
- Leadership conduct: reported in place — Robert requires Nancy to pause a customer export when rights or retention conditions are unresolved. The retained migration-setback decisions show that delivery revenue does not override the handling rules.

Adherence and concerns
- Adherence and reporting: reported in place — Dale samples project conduct acknowledgements and confidential-delivery exceptions. Staff and contractors can raise concerns to Alice or directly to Robert when the normal supervisor is involved.

Responding to departures
- Conduct follow-through: reported in place — Alice assesses concerns with Robert, restricts the affected activity when needed and records a proportionate response. A redacted exercise checks escalation and conflicts; absence of complaints is not used as proof.

ITEMS TO ADDRESS
No confirmation or remediation items were reported in this interview.

Prestige Worldwide reports practices addressing CC7.1 — Configuration and vulnerability detection within the selected system. This is reported readiness, not evidence verification or an auditor opinion.

Configuration changes

- New vulnerability susceptibility detection: reported in place — Snyk scans the selected supported repository manifests for direct and transitive dependency vulnerabilities; provider advisories and endpoint/software inventory cover other components. Owners assess exploitability, patch or justify time-bounded exceptions and validate corrections; SCA alone does not prove secure application code.

OVERVIEW
Prestige Worldwide reports practices addressing CC7.4 — Incident response operation within the selected system. This is reported readiness, not evidence verification or an auditor opinion.

IMPLEMENTATION BREAKDOWN
Defined response and understanding
- Defined response and incident understanding: reported in place — Dale coordinates the response; Brennan establishes the timeline, affected accounts, data and systems; Nancy assesses customer and contract implications. The runbook specifies deputies and escalation to Robert, including uncertain initial scope.

Containment and remediation
- Incident containment: reported in place — Brennan can restrict project access, disable affected identities or credentials, isolate a device and pause an unsafe delivery while preserving investigation records. The team evaluates customer continuity before changing the affected service.
- Incident remediation: reported in place — The responsible owner removes the cause, rotates affected credentials or rebuilds components as needed and tests the corrected behavior. Dale records residual issues and separately validates remediation rather than assuming containment resolves the incident.

Incident communication
- Appropriate incident communication: reported in place — Nancy and Dale prepare factual, authorized notices for the affected customers/providers and internal roles under the applicable commitments. An exercise verifies contact and approval routes; the scenario does not invent a universal notification deadline.

ITEMS TO ADDRESS
No confirmation or remediation items were reported in this interview.

OVERVIEW
Prestige Worldwide reports practices addressing CC8.1 — Authorized system changes within the selected system. This is reported readiness, not evidence verification or an auditor opinion.

IMPLEMENTATION BREAKDOWN
Authorization and design
- Change authorization: reported in place — An accountable owner authorizes the need and scope for infrastructure, application, rights-data and operating-procedure changes. Nancy authorizes customer-rule changes and Brennan authorizes the technical work within delegated limits.
- Change design: reported in place — Design review considers customer/project isolation, confidentiality, retention, capacity, recovery dependencies and rollback. Changes affecting media or rights metadata include the index and delivery interfaces rather than reviewing code in isolation.

Development and configuration
- Change development or acquisition: reported in place — Engineers work in approved repositories and reviewed infrastructure definitions; acquired components receive dependency and supplier checks. Code-assistant output is treated as an untrusted contribution and follows the same review path.
- Change configuration: reported in place — The team checks environment-specific credentials, roles, storage and feature configuration before release. Production settings are compared with the reviewed design; test data and access do not become production defaults.

Documentation and testing
- Change documentation: reported in place — The change record identifies the affected components, migration steps, responsibilities, operating instructions and rollback. Customer handling or recovery instructions are updated with the release and prior versions remain identifiable.
- Change testing: reported in place — Tests exercise intended behavior and relevant failure paths, including cross-project denials, media/rights consistency and rollback. Brennan reviews test results and outstanding exceptions before the release is eligible for approval.

Approval and implementation
- Change approval: reported in place — An authorized reviewer considers the actual proposed change and results before deployment. Configured GitHub rules require reviewing pull requests and named status checks; administrator/bypass paths are included in the rule review and emergency use receives separate follow-up.
- Change implementation: reported in place — An authorized operator follows the approved release sequence, checks health and customer workflows and rolls back if acceptance fails. Emergency changes retain their original reason, operator and later review rather than acquiring a fabricated prior approval.

No confirmation or remediation items were reported in this interview.

- Authorized availability protection design: reported in place — Brennan designs the hosted service, software, media versions, database recovery and protected recovery materials against the four-hour recovery and 24-hour data-loss objectives. - Development, approval, and implementation: reported in place — Robert authorizes the design and resources; Brennan implements the reviewed settings and operators. - Operation and maintenance of availability protections: reported in place — Owners check backup runs, retained versions, recovery credentials, software updates and the full service dependency list. Monitoring the protections
- Monitoring of availability protections: reported in place — Brennan checks failed or stale copies, database backup availability, missing telemetry and recovery-material access. A failed job receives an accountable response and retest; provider storage availability is not treated as evidence that Prestige's backup job succeeded.

assessment_history.implementation:
OVERVIEW
Prestige Worldwide reports practices addressing A1.2 — Resilient operating infrastructure within the selected system. This is reported readiness, not evidence verification or an auditor opinion.

IMPLEMENTATION BREAKDOWN
Authorization and design
- Authorized availability protection design: reported in place — Brennan designs the hosted service, software, media versions, database recovery and protected recovery materials against the four-hour recovery and 24-hour data-loss objectives. AWS environmental responsibilities and Prestige's endpoint/office dependencies are documented separately.

Developed and implemented protections
- Development, approval, and implementation: reported in place — Robert authorizes the design and resources; Brennan implements the reviewed settings and operators. S3 versioning is explicitly enabled; a separate scoped upload workflow sends secondary backup copies to Backblaze B2, not S3 native replication into B2.

Operation and maintenance
- Operation and maintenance of availability protections: reported in place — Owners check backup runs, retained versions, recovery credentials, software updates and the full service dependency list. Lifecycle/deletion rules and permissions are reviewed because versioning alone is neither immutability nor proof that a copy remains recoverable.

Monitoring the protections
- Monitoring of availability protections: reported in place — Brennan checks failed or stale copies, database backup availability, missing telemetry and recovery-material access. A failed job receives an accountable response and retest; provider storage availability is not treated as evidence that Prestige's backup job succeeded.

ITEMS TO ADDRESS
No confirmation or remediation items were reported in this interview.
